hooks.command: echo '[doc-sync] AutoEstate standing rule: CLAUDE.md, TODO.md and the current session-handoff file (session-handoff-YYYY-MM-DD.md at repo root) must always equal the complete current truth, so that a brand-new session reading only those three files knows exactly where things stand. The MOMENT any of these happens, update them immediately (not at end of turn): (1) a TODO item or sub-step completes, becomes blocked or unblocked, gains a new sub-step, or changes order, or a phase changes status; (2) anything changes in the systems this project touches, e.g. Hermes profiles, skills, plugins or gateway config, .env or secrets, the WhatsApp Baileys bridge or its paired number, Telegram, Terraform infra, or the reporting-app (Next.js, Prisma, Clerk, the Hermes state.db it reads from); (3) the user reports outside news, e.g. something changed outside this session, access granted or revoked, a pairing broken, a message sent, a PR merged; (4) a decision is made, a lesson is learned, or a discovered fact contradicts or extends what the docs currently say, including anything deliberately deferred to a later phase and the reasoning for deferring it. Routing, as stated in TODO.md itself: CLAUDE.md owns the brief, phase status, architecture and security decisions, conventions and lessons; TODO.md owns task status, order and sub-checklists; the session-handoff file owns where work stopped and what the next session should pick up first. Do not restate task status in CLAUDE.md or progress narrative in TODO.md. Keep the Last updated line at the top of TODO.md accurate whenever you touch it. Always use absolute dates, never today or yesterday. If a doc statement is now false, correct it rather than appending, and if it was asserted rather than verified, say so. Verify claims about systems you control by running something; confirm claims about what a person said or agreed with the user before acting on them. IMPORTANT - with three files kept in sync, the same fact is usually stated in more than one place, and the handoff file restates status by design. Editing only the file you were working in is the main way these docs go stale. After changing any fact, grep ALL THREE files for the old claim and every other phrasing of it, and fix every copy in the same turn. Respect the git workflow in CLAUDE.md: feature branch and PR into main, never commit doc updates straight to main. If nothing state-changing happened this turn, do nothing.'
